description.content:
The Transaction APIs enable external enterprise customers to ingest and retrieve transaction ledger records within the 73 Strings platform.

These APIs are intended for client-side engineering teams that manage their own data pipelines and require a controlled, structured interface to push transaction data into the platform or retrieve processed transaction information for downstream workflows.

Key capabilities
  • Bulk creation and update of transaction ledger records
  • Platform-generated Display IDs for stable referencing across workflows
  • Retrieval of processed transaction data
  • Reference APIs for transaction types and transaction versions to ensure payload correctness
  • Partial success handling for bulk ingestion
Authentication & data scoping
  • All APIs are authenticated using a subscription key associated with a User ID
  • Organization ID and User ID are mandatory in request payloads and determine data access
  • APIs are multi-tenant by design and return data scoped to the provided organization
Processing model
  • Transactions are pushed via external pipelines (real-time or batch)
  • The platform persists and processes the data as per supported transaction structures
  • The APIs do not orchestrate synchronization or enforce real-time guarantees

item.name: Create or update transactions in bulk (V2)

request.name: Create or update transactions in bulk (V2)

description.content:
Use this endpoint to submit one or more transaction records to the 73 Strings platform in a single JSON request. Each object in TransactionData is validated and processed independently, so a failure for one object does not automatically prevent other valid objects in the same request from being saved.

How create and update are resolved
  • The platform uses multilayeredTransactionMetadata.externalTransactionSourceReferenceId together with the transaction-level asOfDate to decide how each object is processed.
  • If externalTransactionSourceReferenceId is new or not provided, the platform creates a new transaction and generates an internal displayId.
  • If the same externalTransactionSourceReferenceId and the same asOfDate already exist, the existing as-of-date record is fully replaced by the submitted object. This is a full overwrite, not a merge or patch.
  • If the same externalTransactionSourceReferenceId exists with a different asOfDate, the platform creates a new time-series instance under the same logical transaction.
  • Do not send displayId in the request. It is generated and managed by the platform. Use a stable externalTransactionSourceReferenceId for transactions that may need to be updated later.
Request limits and validation
  • A request can include up to 2,000 transaction objects and must not exceed 5 MB.
  • orgId and userId must be authorized for the supplied subscription key.
  • TransactionData is required and must contain at least one object.
  • Dates must use YYYY-MM-DD format. Currency codes must use ISO 4217 three-letter codes, and currency-unit values are case-sensitive.
  • Conditional field groups must be sent completely or omitted completely. For example, local amount fields, reporting amount fields, post-money valuation fields, and security fields should not be partially populated.
  • The same externalTransactionSourceReferenceId plus the same asOfDate must not appear more than once in a single request because the platform cannot determine which object should take precedence.
Response behavior
  • 200 OK means all submitted transaction objects were processed successfully.
  • 207 Multi-Status means at least one object succeeded and at least one object failed validation. Successfully processed objects are saved and are not rolled back; correct and resubmit only the failed objects.
  • If every submitted object fails validation, the response indicates validation failure and no object from that request is saved.
  • If a timeout response is received, verify transaction state before retrying. The server may have processed some or all records before the timeout was returned.

description.content:
The Create Multiple Transactions API allows users to upload multiple transaction records within the 73Strings Transaction Product in a single request.

It supports bulk creation of financial transaction entries such as Investments, Realizations, Valuations, and Fees, with each record tied to an entity, version, and transaction type.

Key capabilities
  • Supports bulk creation of multiple financial transactions in a single API call
  • Validates transaction data at an individual record level
  • Ensures consistency in financial reporting and cross-system integrations
Partial success handling
  • Returns a 207 Multi-Status response when some records are successfully processed
  • Provides detailed validation errors for records that fail processing

description.content:
This API retrieves a list of transaction types configured in the Transaction Product of the 73Strings platform.

It allows clients to fetch transaction type metadata such as ID, name, category, description, and configuration details.

Key details
  • The response supports filtering, sorting, and pagination to optimize data retrieval for different organizational setups.
  • This API is primarily used when clients need to populate dropdowns, map transaction categories, or validate transaction type references before creating transaction data.

query.description: Page number to retrieve (0-indexed). Controls which batch of results is fetched.
Number of records to return per page. Optimizes data retrieval for large lists.

description.content:
The Get Version List API retrieves all available reporting or transaction versions configured within an organization on the 73Strings Transaction Product.

Each version represents a defined data layer (for example, Actuals, Forecast, or Scenario-based data) that is used across financial or transactional modules for reporting and analytics.

This API enables clients to:

  • Fetch all available versions within the organization
  • Identify whether a version is active, fixed, or deletable
  • Integrate version selection into workflows such as creating, editing, or retrieving transactions

description.content:
The Transaction APIs enable external enterprise customers to ingest and retrieve transaction ledger records within the 73 Strings platform.

These APIs are intended for client-side engineering teams that manage their own data pipelines and require a controlled, structured interface to push transaction data into the platform or retrieve processed transaction information for downstream workflows.

Key capabilities
  • Bulk creation and update of transaction ledger records
  • Platform-generated Display IDs for stable referencing across workflows
  • Retrieval of processed transaction data
  • Reference APIs for transaction types and transaction versions to ensure payload correctness
  • Partial success handling for bulk ingestion
Authentication & data scoping
  • All APIs are authenticated using a subscription key associated with a User ID
  • Organization ID and User ID are mandatory in request payloads and determine data access
  • APIs are multi-tenant by design and return data scoped to the provided organization
Processing model
  • Transactions are pushed via external pipelines (real-time or batch)
  • The platform persists and processes the data as per supported transaction structures
  • The APIs do not orchestrate synchronization or enforce real-time guarantees
